ops.body:
**Premise correction before this is implemented — three claims in the description are wrong.** Read this before coding against the task text.

**1. `WaitDelay` alone cannot satisfy criterion `2f72ee23`.** The description calls this "a one-line addition" that "makes the deadline absolute by force-closing the inherited pipes." `WaitDelay` only unblocks `Wait()` — it force-closes the parent's ends of the pipes. The forked grandchild is **not** killed; it orphans and keeps running. So "a test proves a forking child cannot outlast the deadline" is unsatisfiable by the one-line fix as described.

What actually satisfies it is the pattern all five in-repo precedents already use (`internal/web/pdf.go`, `internal/web/browser.go` ×2, `internal/codeexec/discover.go`, `internal/codeexec/driver.go`): `SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true}` **plus** a custom `cmd.Cancel` that SIGKILLs the process *group*, with `WaitDelay` as the backstop. Three parts, not one.

**2. `exec.ErrWaitDelay` will not surface the way the deferral paragraph predicts.** It claims callers get "truncated output plus `ErrWaitDelay` where they currently block indefinitely" on the cancellation path. They will not: `exec.CommandContext` installs a default `Cancel` that kills the process, and it always fires, so `Wait` returns the usual signal `ExitError` instead. `ErrWaitDelay` is reachable only on the *normal-exit-with-a-lingering-descendant* path — a case that previously hung forever, so the change is strictly an improvement there rather than the broad new error shape the deferral was sized against. The stated risk that justified deferring this is largely not real.

**3. `RunCLIExitCodeDir` is the wrong home, and the enumeration scope in `c30a537c` is too narrow.** Putting process-group isolation on `RunCLIExitCodeDir` would change signal semantics for every caller of it, while exactly **one** call site (`internal/cli/lane.go`'s `gtReachable`) runs under a bounded deadline and actually needs it; 6 more are uncancellable cleanup. Criterion `c30a537c` enumerates only `RunCLIExitCode`/`RunCLIExitCodeDir` callers, but `render` has **nine** `RunCLI*` helpers that all share the same constructor line, so any `WaitDelay` change lands on all of them (~115 call sites) regardless of which helper is edited.

**How this is actually being fixed** (in flight, lane `gt-gate`, targeting v0.38.0): `WaitDelay = 5s` moves into a shared `newCmd` used by all nine helpers, and a **tenth** helper `RunCLIProbeDir` carries the process-group isolation via a `render_unix.go`/`render_windows.go` split mirroring `internal/codeexec/discover_unix.go`. Only the probe path gets the changed signal semantics; the other 114 call sites get the `WaitDelay` backstop and nothing else. `gtReachable` switches to `RunCLIProbeDir`.

Criterion `e40fce24` still applies verbatim — the deferral comment on `gtProbeTimeout` is being replaced, though by measurement provenance rather than a pointer to this task.
